stories.headline: What to know before setting your lineup for Week 5: Is Maye back? Start Wilson?
stories.summary: Adam Rank catches you up on the vital information and insight needed to make tough lineup decisions in Week 5.
stories.body:
There seems to be a time in every fantasy football season when we decide to stream a quarterback who seems way too good to be true. And to quote Lt. Aldo Raine, "We hear a story too good to be true ... it ain't." I typically look at streaming quarterbacks in the same light. When the matchup seems too overwhelmingly good, it probably isn't going to work out for you.

I bring this up because last week it was Marcus Mariota. It's almost unfair to bring him up because he was injured early in the contest (and still almost outscored Justin Herbert on the week). But there always seems to be something about streaming a quarterback the entire public has rallied around.

Again, I mention this because everyone has gone wild for Jacoby Brissett because of his matchup with the Lions this week. Even my guy Daniel Dopp has Brissett ranked fifth (at the time of this writing). Again, I will tell you that when you see a matchup too good to be true, it likely is.

I know it's anecdotal, but I've been burned by so many smash quarterback matchups that there isn't an SPF high enough to protect me. I've taken more burns than Super Mario trying to rescue the princess. I've suffered more burns than Jerry Gergich at a Pawnee town hall meeting. I've suffered more burns than ... well, you get the point.

I understand why you want to play Brissett. I mean, it's the Lions. I'm just not sure that I'm ready to do it. And with that, here are some research notes you need to know heading into the big weekend.

Quarterback notes

It should be noted that quarterback scoring was down in Week 4. No quarterback topped 30 points, the leader being Drake Maye (26.16). Is Maye back? The Raiders are middle of the pack in points allowed to quarterbacks this season and top 12 in DVOA, but I'm still rolling with Maye.
One quarterback you might consider benching this week is Jalen Hurts. He has struggled and last week had 93 passing yards, with the Eagles struggling to convert on third down. They traded away offensive lineman Cam Jurgens. Like, are the Eagles trying to win here? I'm curious. I feel like you need to start Hurts because of his rushing potential. But, like English food, I'll indulge, but that doesn't mean I have to like it.
Trevor Lawrence was a low-end QB1 in most fantasy drafts. He's playing excellent football, but he's not a great fantasy quarterback. He's also not great in London, where he has played seven times and scored 14.2 fantasy points per game, including fewer than 20 points in each game. He has won only one game in London when he threw more than one touchdown pass (2024 against the Bears). He also tossed two picks in that one.

Wide receiver notes

I might feel skittish starting Brissett, but I'm loving Michael Wilson. I targeted Wilson over Marvin Harrison Jr. this summer, and it's paying off now. Wilson has scored 42.4 points over the past two weeks, which would make him the No. 6 receiver in fantasy. He leads the NFL in targets (30) and red zone targets (8) over the past two weeks. He absolutely needs to be started.
I do feel good about Harrison, too -- because it's the Lions, not that I think he's back (was he ever there?). But I've targeted Harrison and Brian Thomas Jr. as trade candidates because, well, they are trade candidates in real life. There's a chance (I'm just spit-balling here) either receiver could be sent to a receiver-needy team. I'm still a big believer in their talents, and they could benefit from a change of scenery.
I am buying Carnell Tate. He is trending up, punctuated by 21.5 fantasy points in Week 4. He has close to 30% of the Titans' target share this season. Just give Brian Daboll a little time to cook.
Malik Washington is a potential streaming option for anybody missing one of the Chiefs' or Panthers' pass catchers while they're on bye. He has 10-plus points in back-to-back weeks. The Dolphins' strength of schedule has been ridiculous to start the season. Maybe Miami can get something going as the schedule loosens up. That might even be good news for running back Ollie Gordon II.
Roman Wilson has 31.4 points in his past two games. He has had at least six targets in all four games this season. Do I trust the Steelers yet? I do not.
And finally, I spoke in jest when I said Michael Penix Jr. should be the MVP. But the Falcons look so different with him under center. And he has made Drake London the receiver we all wanted him to be. So I'm cool with it.

stories.headline: Inside a Wrigleyville rooftop owner's fight with the Cubs
stories.summary: Will the last holdout in Wrigleyville be able to stand up to the Chicago Cubs?
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- On a recent night at Wrigley Field, the view from beyond left field was almost perfect. There were the iconic bleachers ... the ivy on the outfield walls ... the field bathed in light. Pete Crow-Armstrong was batting, and the near sellout crowd was chanting: "M-V-P!"

But Aidan Dunican, standing on the rooftop of his four-story apartment building across the street, was pointing out what he couldn't see -- mainly pieces of the infield because of a gauzy, translucent screen affixed to the left-field grandstand that obscured his view, and that of the 50 or so patrons who had paid to watch the game from his rooftop.

The Chicago Cubs installed the screens two seasons ago, along with large letters that advertised a 50-50 raffle that further blocked portions of the field from Dunican. This was no accident: the Cubs sued Dunican and his rooftop business in 2024, arguing he was illegally profiting off their property.

"I was worried it would affect ticket sales," Dunican said in his Irish brogue, while he pointed at the screen. He later added: "People are still coming."

But Dunican now has more pressing concerns than the screens.

On Sept. 30, the same day the Cubs' season ended, a federal judge ruled in favor of the team, ordering Dunican to stop selling tickets to his rooftop -- a victory for the Cubs who have called his operation "parasitic." Dunican told ESPN he is weighing his options for an appeal and intends to continue to fight to keep his 30-year-old business going next season --in what could be considered a quixotic fight against the inevitable or a principled stand for the little guy.

"There's bullying tactics," Dunican said. "And you see how billionaires are pushing around everyone else today. And I live here. So I'm not going to do anything else."

Wrigley, tucked among apartment buildings and residential streets, is a jewel-box park famously part of the neighborhood that bears its name. And part of that charm is the rooftop seating on the apartment buildings just beyond the outfield, which has been a popular destination for fans since the 1990s and the heyday of Sammy Sosa.

The Ricketts family, which owns the Cubs, are like most owners these days, turning their investments into a collection of assets beyond the team itself. The family owns Wrigley Field itself, co-owns the TV network that broadcasts Cubs games and, increasingly, owns the buildings that house the rooftops around Wrigley Field. Ricketts' businesses have bought and acquired 11 buildings and their rooftop businesses surrounding the park. They've reached revenue-sharing deals with others.

Dunican, 64, was the last holdout. He bought his property in the 1990s, knocked down what was there and built a four-story building with two decks of inclined seating on the roof. He lives in the third-floor apartment.

"It's a classic David versus Goliath story and David is being totally squished," said Tom Moore, an attorney who represented a group of rooftop owners more than a decade ago in negotiations with the Cubs and the city. Most of his clients ended up selling to the Ricketts.

Of Dunican, Moore said: "I wish him well. Usually Goliath beats up David."

Somewhere between $100 and $300 got you a seat at Dunican's Wrigley View Rooftop, along with an open bar until the seventh inning and all the Chicago-style hot dogs and Italian beef sandwiches you could eat. The rooftop holds around 200 people, and if Dunican didn't sell 50 tickets for a game, he usually wouldn't open.

Dunican said the business usually generates around $1 million annually before accounting for expenses. Until 2024, he was paying the Cubs around 17% royalties due to a 2004 agreement signed by all the rooftops in business at the time.

When that deal expired after the 2023 season, Dunican hoped to extend it. The Cubs said no, Dunican said. He offered 20% of his gross revenue, but the Cubs wanted 30% for regular-season games and 40% for postseason games, he said. "It would have put me out of business," he said.

The Cubs argued Dunican needed an agreement with the team to profit off the games. They paid nearly a billion dollars to refurbish the stadium plus hundreds of millions more annually on running the team and Wrigley upkeep every year. Any money spent with Dunican might be spent on tickets and concessions inside the park, they argued. (The Cubs also argued Dunican was misusing their logo on marketing materials, which Dunican acknowledged.)

Dunican countered that if the Cubs are so offended by his business they should block his view more completely. Further, he said, the city gave him a license to operate his rooftop specifically during Cubs games.

The court was unmoved by those arguments, emphatically siding with the Cubs. "Unfairly capitalizing on another's labor and expenses offends principles of justice, equity, and good conscience," federal judge Sharon Johnson Coleman wrote in her Sept. 30 ruling.

"The decision protects our intellectual property rights and affirms our longstanding position that businesses cannot commercially profit from Cubs games or use Cubs intellectual property without authorization," the Cubs wrote in a statement after the decision. (The team declined to comment further on the case.)

Dunican, standing on his rooftop before the judge's decision, posed another question, less legal and more philosophical: How much of Wrigleyville do the Cubs have a right to control?

He pointed out where a carwash had been that was now a glitzy Cubs office building, and a McDonald's is now a Ricketts-owned boutique hotel. Yum Yum Donuts had given way to Gallagher Way, an entertainment plaza that requires a ticket on Cubs game days. The Cubs' revenue-sharing proposal to him also included a right of first refusal on a sale of both his rooftop building and any other property Dunican owned within a mile of Wrigley. (He owned one other building, which he has since sold.)

It's a question that gets to the heart of a growing trend in sports: franchises as real estate empires. In 2017, the Atlanta Braves opened The Battery Atlanta around their stadium -- a "ballpark village" complete with restaurants, shops and apartments. The St. Louis Cardinals partnered with a development company to build a group of bars and restaurants next to their stadium. When Stan Kroenke reached a deal to acquire the Los Angeles Angels last month, there was widespread belief that the team fetched $4 billion dollars because of the value of the land around the ballpark.

After the Ricketts family bought the Cubs, businesses they owned started scooping up the rooftop buildings and launched their own rooftop business. The buildings usually went for a few million dollars. (Dunican said no one connected to the Cubs made him a formal offer to buy his building.)

Moore, the attorney who used to represent many of the rooftop businesses, said those sales often happened after the Cubs threatened to block the views. But the Cubs were both aided by multiple court rulings, and the city approved the construction. Plus, the team believed it was its intellectual property to monetize.

They've also expanded in Wrigleyville. The team recently opened a new merchandise store in a former CVS across the street from the stadium and next to another merchandise store that has been in business for decades. If you buy a Cubs hat, the Cubs also would like your $30.

"If you're a team, it's your asset," said Tim Katt, who leads the sports practice at commercial real estate company Transwestern. "You're the one driving the traffic so you should be capturing the dollars from the consumers. You want them buying an $8 beer in your stadium versus the bar next door."

When Wrigley was under construction, Dunican recalled that Crane Kenney, Cubs president of business operations, used to walk by Dunican's building and heckle him as he passed.

"It was never a 'Good morning,' Dunican said. "It was, 'We're going to block you' and 'You're going to lose your property, anyway.'" (A Cubs spokesperson denied Kenney said this.)

"Aidan is thankful for what the Cubs have built," said Sean Duffy, another friend of Dunican's. "But at the same time, the Cubs are benefiting from the neighborhood."

On a recent night, as the Cubs and the Braves battled in a September pennant race, Dunican flitted around his building, doing all sorts of jobs. A bar back called out sick so he went to buy beer. He checked guests in at the front door and mixed a few drinks behind the bar. Aside from a few part-time employees, he runs the business mostly himself.

Dunican grew up in the Irish countryside near Tullamore, where his father was a cattle farmer. He moved to Chicago after a year of college where several family members already lived, and has been here since 1981. Dunican worked construction and did well enough to buy a few properties, fix them up and rent them out. On a construction job in the late '90s, he noticed a property on Waveland Avenue next to Wrigley for sale.

He paid $400,000 for the building, planning to turn it into high-end condos, but during construction he noticed the views and the nascent rooftop businesses. Today, he lives on the third floor, rents another apartment on Airbnb and the top three floors host rooftop guests. (Each summer, he hosts a group of young Irish kids on work visas for several weeks.)

"I don't know how to describe him," his friend, Carl Madonia, said. "He's an Irish guy. He's a regular guy."

"He really doesn't talk much," said Marilyn Knaus, a lifelong Wrigleyville resident who has been working for Dunican for several years as a bartender.

But Knaus recognized something in Dunican that she also feels: a love of the neighborhood. Her husband worked at the fire station next door and firefighters, working their shifts, come over to visit once in a while.

"It's hard to leave the neighborhood," Knaus said. "It's hard to leave the people. No one's ever in a bad mood when they come here."

Still, Dunican must now confront the possibility that a new Cubs season will come next spring without his rooftop business. Maybe he can pivot the business into a restaurant and bar (though his business license right now limits any days he can be open beyond Cubs games). Maybe he could sell to a wealthy person who wants to live next to Wrigley. Or a developer who wants to put up condos.

Asked if he would sell to the Ricketts family, Dunican said: "I'd have to consider if it was a fair offer."

He declined to say what a fair offer would be, but noted he put more than $2 million into the building in 2010 in further renovations.

On the rooftop that September night, Dunican said he remembered sitting at the bar when the Cubs won the World Series in 2016. He didn't grow up watching baseball, but he was a big Cubs fan now, and not just because of the business. He still goes to an occasional game. Crow-Armstrong is his favorite player.

As he considered how he'd spend this offseason, he noted that last year he traveled back to Ireland to visit family and the farm where he grew up.

"It's changed there," he said. "Nothing stays the same there, either."

stories.headline: Jalen Duren, Pistons need each other -- for better or worse
stories.summary: After agreeing to a five-year, $200 million deal, how will Duren and Detroit move forward after a monthslong saga?
stories.body:
Deciding whether to bring back Jalen Duren was only the second biggest question for the Detroit Pistons this offseason, as they size up a vastly different Eastern Conference than the one that saw them run away with 60 wins and the No. 1 seed last season.

The monthslong saga with Duren was over money, of course, but also power and respect. A lack of personal touch and a very direct -- if not harsh -- approach to the negotiations was one of the reasons it lasted so long. Duren's underperformance during the playoffs -- he averaged just 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds over 14 games -- combined with these protracted talks didn't leave a great taste with anyone.

Duren's postseason performance exposed the oversized weight MVP candidate Cade Cunningham carried, as the guard had nine games of five turnovers or more, illustrating the need for another premier shot creator. The Pistons inquired about trading for Kawhi Leonard and Kevin Durant this offseason, according to league sources, and were positioned to offer Austin Reaves a big free agent contract if the Los Angeles Lakers opened the door. None of that materialized.

The Pistons had heard Leonard wasn't interested in coming to Detroit amid the Clippers' cap-circumvention scandal, per league sources, and the Rockets weren't willing to engage on Durant despite the close relationship he shares with Cunningham. As for Reaves, once the Lakers blew him away with a max contract offer, he wasn't going anywhere -- he'd already turned down being drafted by Detroit under the Troy Weaver era to go the undrafted route and sign with the Lakers a few years ago.

Instead, the Pistons were left with Duren, who was facing the double whammy of big playoff failure and restricted free agency. For most of the offseason, the Pistons were offering a deal starting in the range of $30 million per year, a slight step down from the $40 million he eventually got. If his feelings are indeed bothered by this process, will the cold, hard cash of $200 million over five years be the balm?

"Looking in the mirror, I do need to get better," Duren said Sunday at the team's facility announcing his contract. "I'm man enough to acknowledge my flaws and I'm man enough to acknowledge that I'm not perfect, and I'm also man enough to get my ass in the gym and work on those things and get better."

Duren is 22, and as the NBA has shown for 80 years with very few exceptions, players fail and fail early. Sometimes embarrassingly. It doesn't guarantee success on the back end, but Duren was provided a blueprint for what works and what doesn't when the weather turns warm, the scouting report gets thick and pet plays are taken away.

The East is filled with brand names at the top and teams that are no longer incentivized to lose at the bottom. The Philadelphia 76ers reloaded by adding two Finals MVPs, including the generational LeBron James, who seems motivated for ring No. 5. Tyrese Haliburton returns to the Indiana Pacers after missing last season with a right Achilles tear, and Giannis Antetokounmpo poses a major threat as he's paired with the organizational know-how the Miami Heat provide.

And let's not forget the champion New York Knicks.

An All-Star, All-NBA-worthy center in Duren is the minimum the Pistons require: They need him at his absolute best just to compete in this newly configured conference.

Sources tell ESPN one of the reasons for Duren's frustration was hearing in negotiations that he was the team's fourth-best player -- perhaps said in a way to illustrate how far he'd fallen in the playoffs, perhaps the cold part of negotiations.

Duren's regular season included a stretch in which he kept the Pistons atop the East when Cunningham was out with a collapsed lung, and culminated in him becoming the third Piston in franchise history to be All-NBA at his age or younger (joining Isiah Thomas in 1982-83, 84 and Andre Drummond in 2015-16). But the playoffs were another story.

He went from averaging 19.5 PPG in the regular season to 10.2 PPG in the postseason. That 9.3 drop in PPG was the third-largest scoring decrease from a regular season to postseason in NBA history by a player selected as an All-Star, trailing Wilt Chamberlain and Elgin Baylor.

"Last season was some of my highest moments in my career and some of my lowest," Duren said on Sunday. "I'm willing to acknowledge that. And I'm willing to turn that frustration and that anger and whatever I felt toward my play and how things may have ended, I've learned instead of exerting my energy in being mad, exerting my energy into bettering my craft."

The playoffs were ugly, as Duren was outplayed by big men Wendell Carter Jr. of the Orlando Magic and Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen of the Cleveland Cavaliers.

When word got back to Duren that his playoff performance had hurt his standing in the organization, he began exploring his market value -- though many in the organization believed Duren would eventually return. Despite being a restricted free agent, he met with the Sacramento Kings early into free agency. The Atlanta Hawks, Milwaukee Bucks and Washington Wizards also had interest, sources tell ESPN.

But Detroit had the inside track. It knew that whatever number it landed on would be greater than whatever was outside its doors -- and the Pistons were unwilling to engage on a sign-and-trade, league sources tell ESPN.

Duren's game has grown since he was drafted: As a big who can handle the ball, an improving defender and perhaps a midrange jump shooter. That isn't easy to find in this league, and the Pistons know it. He and Cunningham have developed great chemistry and been catalysts in Detroit's turnaround, and there aren't many lead guards Duren can find who are better.

Unlike many other Eastern contenders, the Pistons aren't cash-strapped: Detroit entered the offseason having signed two players to contracts worth at least $100 million, the fewest in the NBA (both Cunningham and Drummond on max rookie extensions).

For the Pistons, whether they brought back Ausar Thompson on a lower-than-expected number for 2027-28 and beyond only mattered so much. Over the past two weeks, they have agreed to deals with Duren ($200 million) and Thompson ($155 million), doubling the previous offseason total.

Their three best players are still on the upswing, and they have all of their future draft picks to use in a trade should the opportunity arise.

Once players on rookie deals start getting rewarded, the clock starts ticking. It's just a fact of second aprons and natural progressions. The Pistons have bet big on Duren and Thompson's development, even though they haven't bet the house on them. Thompson could very well be the league's best defender this side of San Antonio and was a terror in the playoffs.

Team president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon wanted to see how last year's youth-laden team would perform within the cauldron of the playoffs, resisting an all-in move. Conventional wisdom stated the hellacious defense from the regular season didn't have another level to reach, and that belief was correct, hence the struggle.

So, Langdon has tried to operate around the margins. No blockbuster moves. There didn't appear to be real traction toward bringing Tobias Harris back, and the Pistons and Isaiah Stewart equally seemed ready for a change, meaning a big part of this identity was willfully being stripped.

Bringing in John Collins to replace Harris means they got a little younger, and they added shooting in Oklahoma City's Isaiah Joe and perhaps veteran Taurean Prince if he's healthy -- all three are on deals the Pistons can get out of after the season. And most importantly, Langdon brought back Thompson and Duren for less than the max.

As it stands, it feels like the Pistons aren't in the top playoff tier with Philadelphia and New York, but their sweat equity means they should win their share of regular-season games. And if Detroit has the stomach to go after it this year, they could go after someone like Kyrie Irving in Dallas -- several staffers are fond of Irving's game, shot creation and malleability next to ball-dominant stars like James and Luka Doncic.

If a high-revenue team like the Knicks is pinching pennies, it means everybody else will follow suit in some ways. But the Knicks won a title before their cost-cutting moves. So did the Thunder before trading away three key pieces.

Detroit fans have just gotten used to being good again, so the in-town expectations are not willing to cede ground to Philadelphia or Miami just because those teams acquired big names with championship pedigrees. Duren got his money, as painful as the process was.

Now, it's on him and the team to make sure that wasn't a preview of the struggle to come in the regular season ... or beyond.

stories.headline: How Angel Reese is taking starring role in WNBA playoff debut
stories.summary: The forward has played just four playoff games but is playing like a vet in leading Atlanta to a 2-0 lead in the semis.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- Angel Reese was playing in just her fourth WNBA playoff game. But with 6.1 seconds left in overtime, her Atlanta Dream squad clinging to a one-point lead and the New York Liberty looking to foul, she knew exactly what to do.

Reese raced to the sideline and whispered in teammate DeWanna Bonner's ear to inbound the ball in the backcourt -- which is only allowed in the final two minutes -- so Reese could kill some clock.

The end of Wednesday's Game 2 semifinal was marred by controversy over why New York didn't call its final reset timeout, but it overshadowed Reese's sneaky and savvy move that preceded the ordeal: She ran 1.8 seconds off the clock and drew the sixth and final foul on hot-shooting Liberty rookie Marine Fauthoux.

Reese converted both free throws, Breanna Stewart missed a last-ditch heave, the buzzer sounded and Reese and Bonner shared a long embrace on the court. With the win, the Dream secured a 2-0 series lead in the best-of-five series.

The play might not even make Reese's highlight reel from the night as Atlanta won its ninth consecutive game. She scored a playoff career-high 23 points, had a team-best six of them in overtime and added seven rebounds and two blocks, including an emphatic volleyball-esque rejection on Sabrina Ionescu in the fourth quarter. In one memorable sequence in the second period, Reese made a 3-pointer before stealing the ball seconds later, driving back down the floor and converting an and-1 sequence that gave the Dream the lead.

With contributions obvious and subtle, Reese has helped transform the No. 4-seeded Dream into arguably the best team remaining in the WNBA playoffs -- at the very least the only one yet to lose in the 2026 postseason -- and one win away from returning to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013.

"She's the motor," said Bonner, a 39-year-old vet in her 17th WNBA season. "Her defensive presence is unmatched. ... She brings the toughness. She brings the umph. As long as she's out there, we see her go hard, it's like, 'Man, I want to dive on the floor for a ball.'

"That's rare. That's kind of hard to find ... we feed off her, and she gets us going every single game."

The No. 7 pick by the Chicago Sky in the 2024 WNBA draft, Reese has had a remarkable start to her pro career, earning All-Star honors in each of her first three seasons and establishing herself to potentially be the best rebounder in WNBA history.

The Sky made a stunning move in April when they traded Reese to the Dream following some friction between her and the team, including when Reese told a local outlet during the 2025 season that Chicago needed to get great players in the offseason or she might consider moving on.

The Sky would embark on a roster revamp, but in Atlanta, Reese was immediately surrounded by more talent than ever before. The fit on and off the court proved seamless.

Reese has been featured alongside fellow young stars Rhyne Howard (a former No. 1 pick and a four-time All-Star) and Naz Hillmon, both of whom Atlanta drafted in 2022. Thirty-one-year-olds Allisha Gray, also a four-time All-Star, and Jordin Canada, a two-time WNBA champion, arrived in 2023 and 2024, respectively, via trade.

"When you play with great players, they push you every single day to your potential, maybe even more," Reese said. "And I'm just so grateful for my teammates. I'm grateful for my coaches every single day. We have fun, we have hard conversations. They love on me, and they're just there for me all the time.

"I'm just really thankful for it because you don't really get the opportunity [always]. I haven't had that in a while, and being able to be here in Atlanta, I'm just really grateful to have sisters in the locker room that really, really genuinely care and love me."

Gray, Howard and Reese were the Dream's big three in the regular season, each averaging at least 15 points. Reese led the league in rebounding for the third year in a row (12.1 per game), won her first Defensive Player of the Year award and helped Atlanta achieve the third-best defensive rating -- all while bringing intangibles to her new team.

"Angel is definitely a huge part of what we do, and her energy is contagious," Atlanta coach Karl Smesko said. "She's definitely an emotional leader for us."

When the playoffs opened in late September, nerves weren't entirely avoidable for Reese in the first round. "That 1-1-1 [format] is scary, I'm not gonna lie," Reese said Sunday. But she tried to remind herself she has been in plenty of high-stakes situations, such as winning a national championship her junior season at LSU.

"I have been in experiences where it's win or go home, and that's kind of how I'm treating every game [in the playoffs]," Reese said. "I don't want to rely on five games. I want to be able to win, win, win, win and then move on to the next round."

Reese added to her trophy case last month at the FIBA World Cup, where she won a gold medal with USA Basketball and boasted the fifth-best efficiency on a team stacked with All-WNBA talent.

"This may be her first playoffs, but I told her she's a championship player," said Howard, who was also on Team USA. "On all of her other levels, she's done this, and she has that experience that some of us don't have, and so we're also leaning on her. She's been that dog for us all season."

Even in an unfamiliar setting when the lights are brightest, Reese knew she could lean on the qualities that have always separated her from her peers.

"I always talk about you can't be scared when it comes to this," Reese said. "When I played against the Mystics [in the first round], I knew I was just going to be fearless. Go out there and play fearless. Play relentless. Play with just so much poise and just have fun and do everything I can do. And that's always how I've been in my career."

In the playoffs, Reese is averaging 17.0 points, 8.3 rebounds, 2.3 blocks and 1.8 steals, but her impact is felt well beyond the box score. The Dream's plus-21.6 net efficiency with Reese on the floor is the best of any player this postseason (minimum 10 minutes).

"She's locked in, like locked in," Hillmon said, adding that it's a reflection of how Reese competes on a daily basis. "I think that's just the way that Angel plays all the time. She doesn't have to get up for moments because she's already up."

Reese's defensive impact is even more staggering: Opponents are shooting 37% (11 of 30) this postseason with Reese as the defender; that percentage is even lower in the semifinals, where she's holding the Liberty to 5-of-16 shooting (31.2%) through two games, including 2-for-6 from Stewart.

Atlanta has a defensive efficiency of 91.9 in the postseason with her on the court, the best of any player with at least 35 minutes.

"When she's at her best she can be incredibly disruptive, maybe the most disruptive player defensively in the league," Smesko said. "And that's probably why she won Defensive Player of the Year."

Reese likes to write down her objectives heading into a season, starting with team goals before heading into individual ones. This year with the Dream, making the playoffs was practically a given. Earning her first gold medal in Berlin with the senior national team was a big ambition to check off. Defensive Player of the Year was also there.

If she has her way, that won't be the last goal she'll have manifested this season.

"A championship would mean everything to me," Reese said Sunday, "and we're not done yet."

ESPN Research contributed to this report.

stories.headline: NHL Power Rankings: Each team's NHL Rank representatives
stories.summary: It's the first regular-season update of our 1-32 poll. Plus, how many players did each team land among the Top 100?
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NHL season is 10 days old, but what a wild campaign it's been so far.

There have been exciting debuts by a number of rookies, a goalie goal by Igor Shesterkin, and an incredible scoring display by Oilers stars Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard.

This week also included the release of ESPN's annual NHL Rank, which listed the top 100 players for the coming season as voted on by a panel of broadcasters, reporters and analysts.

Along with an updated 1-32 poll here, let's take a look at who from each team was represented in that Top 100 for 2026-27.

How we rank: A panel of ESPN hockey commentators, analysts, reporters and editors sends in a 1-32 poll based on the games through Wednesday. Those ballots are combined to come up with the rankings you see below.

Note: Previous ranking for each team refers to the preseason preview, which published on Sept. 28. Points percentages are through Thursday's games.

1. Colorado Avalanche
Previous ranking: 2

Points percentage: 75%

As one of the top teams in the league, it's not surprising that the Avs landed five players on the list: Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Martin Necas, Mackenzie Blackwood and Devon Toews.

Next seven days: vs. TOR (Oct. 10), @ DAL (Oct. 13), vs. DAL (Oct. 14)

2. Utah Mammoth
Previous ranking: 11

Points percentage: 60%

Off to perhaps a surprisingly hot start, the Mammoth have four Top 100 players this year: Clayton Keller, Dylan Guenther, Logan Cooley and Mikhail Sergachev.

Next seven days: @ BUF (Oct. 10), vs. TOR (Oct. 13), @ EDM (Oct. 15)

3. Vegas Golden Knights
Previous ranking: 5

Points percentage: 80%

Despite an appearance in the 2026 Stanley Cup Final, just four Golden Knights cracked the Top 100: Jack Eichel, Mitch Marner, Mark Stone and Shea Theodore.

Next seven days: vs. LA (Oct. 10), @ MIN (Oct. 12), @ NSH (Oct. 13), vs. CGY (Oct. 15)

4. Minnesota Wild
Previous ranking: 6

Points percentage: 62.5%

The Wild landed two players in the top 10 (Quinn Hughes and Kirill Kaprizov), another in the top 20 (Matt Boldy) and one further down the charts -- the currently injured Brock Faber, at No. 72.

Next seven days: @ FLA (Oct. 10), vs. VGK (Oct. 12), @ WPG (Oct. 13), vs. STL (Oct. 15)

5. New York Rangers
Previous ranking: 25

Points percentage: 80%

Given the Blueshirts' start, perhaps our NHL Rank voters underestimated the talent on the roster, with just two making the list: Igor Shesterkin and Adam Fox.

Next seven days: @ WSH (Oct. 9), vs. VAN (Oct. 11), vs. TB (Oct. 13), @ NJ (Oct. 15)

6. Edmonton Oilers
Previous ranking: 9

Points percentage: 87.5%

Those three superstars mentioned in the intro? That's it for the Oilers on the Top 100, although McDavid and Draisaitl were among the top six.

Next seven days: @ SJ (Oct. 10), @ LA (Oct. 13), vs. UTA (Oct. 15)

7. Florida Panthers
Previous ranking: 4

Points percentage: 75%

Poised for another serious run at the Stanley Cup, the Panthers will do so with four top-50 players: Matthew Tkachuk, Aleksander Barkov, Sam Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk.

Next seven days: vs. MIN (Oct. 10), @ BUF (Oct. 12), @ CBJ (Oct. 13), vs. VAN (Oct. 15)

8. Carolina Hurricanes
Previous ranking: 1

Points percentage: 70%

The Cup champs have found success in recent seasons with a "superstar-free" approach, sending waves upon waves at opponents. Five Canes made the Top 100 this year: Sebastian Aho, Jaccob Slavin, Seth Jarvis, Andrei Svechnikov and Nikolaj Ehlers.

Next seven days: @ CHI (Oct. 10), @ PHI (Oct. 11), vs. WSH (Oct. 13)

9. Anaheim Ducks
Previous ranking: 14

Points percentage: 66.7%

The Ducks have an exciting (and now quite wealthy) young core group, and three members of it made the list: Leo Carlsson, Jackson LaCombe and Cutter Gauthier.

Next seven days: @ WPG (Oct. 9), @ CGY (Oct. 10), vs. CGY (Oct. 13)

10. Tampa Bay Lightning
Previous ranking: 8

Points percentage: 75%

Our voters clearly still believe that Tampa Bay's contention window is wide open, with six Lightning players in the Top 100: Nikita Kucherov, Andrei Vasilevskiy, Jake Guentzel, Brandon Hagel, Brayden Point and Victor Hedman.

Next seven days: @ NYI (Oct. 10), @ NYR (Oct. 13), vs. SEA (Oct. 15)

11. Pittsburgh Penguins
Previous ranking: 20

Points percentage: 50%

Just three Penguins made the list this year, and you can probably envision them before reading this list: Sidney Crosby, Erik Karlsson and Evgeni Malkin.

Next seven days: @ CBJ (Oct. 9), vs. DAL (Oct. 10), @ CHI (Oct. 13)

12. Winnipeg Jets
Previous ranking: 28

Points percentage: 87.5%

Yes, Connor Hellebuyck made the list -- so clearly our voters believe he'll be suiting up for someone at some point this season. In addition to the netminder, Mark Scheifele, Kyle Connor and Josh Morrissey made the cut.

Next seven days: vs. ANA (Oct. 9), vs. MIN (Oct. 13), @ CHI (Oct. 15)

13. Ottawa Senators
Previous ranking: 19

Points percentage: 75%

With Brady Tkachuk now on the Panthers, the Sens have come out of the gates strong. However, our voters didn't give them much love, with just two players landing in the Top 100: Jake Sanderson and Tim Stutzle.

Next seven days: vs. NSH (Oct. 10), @ NJ (Oct. 12), vs. STL (Oct. 13), vs. NYI (Oct. 15)

14. Buffalo Sabres
Previous ranking: 10

Points percentage: 50%

Is Western New York prepared for another playoff run? The Sabres' two reps on the Rank list -- Rasmus Dahlin and Tage Thompson -- will keep pushing them toward that goal.

Next seven days: vs. UTA (Oct. 10), vs. FLA (Oct. 12), @ MTL (Oct. 13), @ TOR (Oct. 15)

15. Washington Capitals
Previous ranking: 12

Points percentage: 66.7%

It's Alex Ovechkin's final NHL season, and yes, he made his final NHL Rank list as well. He is joined by teammates Logan Thompson, Jakob Chychrun and Tom Wilson.

Next seven days: vs. NYR (Oct. 9), vs. SEA (Oct. 11), @ CAR (Oct. 13), vs. MTL (Oct. 14)

16. Seattle Kraken
Previous ranking: 30

Points percentage: 50%

Well, when you have 32 teams in the league and only 100 spots on a rankings list, there are bound to be teams that don't land anyone there. Such is the case for the Kraken (and two other clubs) this season.

Next seven days: @ DET (Oct. 9), @ WSH (Oct. 11), @ PHI (Oct. 13), @ TB (Oct. 15)

17. Dallas Stars
Previous ranking: 3

Points percentage: 50%

Much like the Lightning, ESPN's voters believe the veteran-laden Stars are also firmly in a contention window. Like Tampa Bay, Dallas landed six players on the list: Mikko Rantanen, Jason Robertson, Wyatt Johnston, Miro Heiskanen, Jake Oettinger and Thomas Harley.

Next seven days: @ PIT (Oct. 10), vs. COL (Oct. 13), @ COL (Oct. 14)

18. San Jose Sharks
Previous ranking: 13

Points percentage: 75%

One of the surprises of the poll was Macklin Celebrini landing at No. 4 overall in his third NHL season. Just one other Shark made the cut this year: Will Smith.

Next seven days: vs. EDM (Oct. 10), vs. BOS (Oct. 13), @ NSH (Oct. 15)

19. Boston Bruins
Previous ranking: 17

Points percentage: 60%

The Bruins have been a bit up and down this season, but the skill level of their "Big 3" is not in question; our voters agreed, electing David Pastrnak, Charlie McAvoy and Jeremy Swayman to the list.

Next seven days: vs. PHI (Oct. 10), @ SJ (Oct. 13)

20. Montreal Canadiens
Previous ranking: 7

Points percentage: 37.5%

One of the other surprises -- to some -- is the fact that six Canadiens made the Top 100, tying the Stars and Lightning for the most by a team. But who can argue against Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson, Juraj Slafkovsky, Noah Dobson or Ivan Demidov?

Next seven days: vs. DET (Oct. 10), vs. BUF (Oct. 13), @ WSH (Oct. 14)

21. Toronto Maple Leafs
Previous ranking: 18

Points percentage: 50%

For years, the Leafs were led by the "Core Four." Perhaps they have a new one, centered around Auston Matthews, William Nylander, Kirill Marchenko and Darren Raddysh?

Next seven days: @ COL (Oct. 10), @ UTA (Oct. 13), vs. BUF (Oct. 15)

22. Columbus Blue Jackets
Previous ranking: 23

Points percentage: 50%

It's no shock that Zach Werenski made the list (and landed in the top 10). But a pleasant surprise for Jackets fans is that youngsters Adam Fantilli and Matthew Knies join him in the Top 100.

Next seven days: vs. PIT (Oct. 9), @ STL (Oct. 10), vs. FLA (Oct. 13)

23. New York Islanders
Previous ranking: 22

Points percentage: 50%

Like Celebrini at No. 4, Matthew Schaefer landing at No. 16 raised some eyebrows among analysts and league insiders this week. The reigning Calder Trophy winner is joined by teammates Ilya Sorokin, Bo Horvat and Mathew Barzal.

Next seven days: vs. TB (Oct. 10), vs. VAN (Oct. 13), @ OTT (Oct. 15)

24. Nashville Predators
Previous ranking: 26

Points percentage: 62.5%

A trio of veterans made the cut this year, all in the 51-100 range after prior appearances in much higher slots: Filip Forsberg, Roman Josi and Steven Stamkos.

Next seven days: @ OTT (Oct. 10), vs. VGK (Oct. 13), vs. SJ (Oct. 15)

25. Vancouver Canucks
Previous ranking: 32

Points percentage: 40%

It shouldn't be too shocking to learn that last season's basement dwellers landed zero players in the Top 100. But given how hot some of them have started on the score sheet, perhaps it'll be quite a different story in the spring.

Next seven days: @ NJ (Oct. 10), @ NYR (Oct. 11), @ NYI (Oct. 13), @ FLA (Oct. 15)

26. Detroit Red Wings
Previous ranking: 27

Points percentage: 33.3%

It was a rough offseason for the Red Wings, with trade requests and contract holdouts and still no permanent general manager. But there's hope, with four Wings in the Top 100: Moritz Seider, Alex DeBrincat, Lucas Raymond and Dylan Larkin (who may be wearing a different sweater before season's end).

Next seven days: vs. SEA (Oct. 9), @ MTL (Oct. 10), vs. NJ (Oct. 13), vs. PHI (Oct. 15)

27. New Jersey Devils
Previous ranking: 15

Points percentage: 33.3%

Should we start saying that the Devils have a Big 3 as well? That's the group that made the Top 100, including Jack Hughes, Nico Hischier and Jesper Bratt.

Next seven days: vs. VAN (Oct. 10), vs. OTT (Oct. 12), @ DET (Oct. 13), vs. NYR (Oct. 15)

28. St. Louis Blues
Previous ranking: 24

Points percentage: 37.5%

For a team that narrowly missed the 2026 playoffs, one would think the Blues would land more players in the Top 100. Alas, it's just Robert Thomas and Dylan Holloway.

Next seven days: vs. CBJ (Oct. 10), @ OTT (Oct. 13), @ MIN (Oct. 15)

29. Los Angeles Kings
Previous ranking: 21

Points percentage: 16.7%

As the Kings begin the post-Anze Kopitar era, they do so with three Top 100 players: Artemi Panarin, Adrian Kempe and Brandt Clarke.

Next seven days: @ VGK (Oct. 10), vs. EDM (Oct. 13)

30. Chicago Blackhawks
Previous ranking: 29

Points percentage: 20%

Just one Blackhawk makes the list, and you can probably guess which one it was: Connor Bedard, who landed at No. 43 overall.

Next seven days: vs. CAR (Oct. 10), vs. PIT (Oct. 13), vs. WPG (Oct. 15)

31. Philadelphia Flyers
Previous ranking: 16

Points percentage: 20%

Perhaps surprisingly, only one Flyer made the list, too -- and it might not be the one you're picturing. Trevor Zegras is Philly's lone rep in the Top 100.

Next seven days: @ BOS (Oct. 10), vs. CAR (Oct. 11), vs. SEA (Oct. 13), @ DET (Oct. 15)

32. Calgary Flames
Previous ranking: 31

Points percentage: 0%

Amid an acknowledged period of rebuilding, contention appears distant for the Flames. And so it follows that they did not place any players in the Top 100 this season.

Next seven days: vs. ANA (Oct. 10), @ ANA (Oct. 13), @ VGK (Oct. 15)

stories.headline: Singapore Grand Prix: George Russell sets pace in sole practice session ahead of sprint qualifying
stories.summary: George Russell topped the timesheets in the first and only practice session at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
George Russell topped the timesheets in the first and only practice session at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The Mercedes driver set a time of 1:32.274 on the soft tyre, just under two-tenths quicker than Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

McLaren's Lando Norris rounded out the top three, with Lewis Hamilton in fourth in what was hazy conditions in daylight around the Marina Bay Circuit.

Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren finished fifth-fastest, half a second off the leader's pace.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who claimed his first win of the season last weekend at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, crossed the line in sixth.

A yellow flag was waved in the closing stages of the session after Kimi Antonelli went off at Turn 16, but he managed to get going again. The Italian youngster finished down the order in seventh.

Antonelli is running the upgraded Mercedes specification this weekend as he bids to extend his lead in the drivers' championship, while Russell has reverted to the previous package.

- When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races

- Rwanda F1 race: Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen welcome prospect of Africa return as talks gather pace

- George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to run different Mercedes packages at Singapore Grand Prix

But despite Russell going quickest in first practice, he will start Sunday's race at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty.

Verstappen's teammate Isack Hadjar finished in eighth and reported on the team radio that he had no confidence in the car.

Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson were ninth and 10th respectively.

Singapore makes its sprint weekend debut and qualifying for Saturday's sprint race goes green at 1.30 p.m. BST / 8.30 a.m. ET.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No.12 and No.31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No.4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No.6 and No.10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No.4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No.39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Jake Paul cleared to fight; Canelo, Strickland, others on wish list
stories.summary: Jake Paul, who has been cleared to resume fighting after recovering from a broken jaw, has a list of big names he'd like to face in boxing and MMA now that he's back.
stories.body:
Jake Paul has been medically cleared to return to boxing.

Paul (12-2, seven KOs), 29, has not fought since he suffered a broken jaw during his knockout loss to Anthony Joshua last December. Paul underwent surgical procedures on his jaw in December and February. Nakisa Bidarian, co-founder of Paul's Most Valuable Promotions, officially updated Paul's status Thursday.

"Jake Paul has been cleared to return to the boxing ring," Bidarian wrote on X.

Paul told ESPN in April that he'd resumed light training but had not been cleared to spar. He has targeted a full return to competition in early 2027.

In connection to the update on his health, Paul provided his latest wish list of eventual fights this week. The list included 15 potential fights, including Canelo Alvarez, Ryan Garcia, Francis Ngannou, Deontay Wilder in boxing as well as mixed martial arts contests against Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz.

The list also included UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland (31-7), who linked himself to Paul this week in a series of online posts expressing frustration about his UFC contract.

"I gotta be honest, unless things change with the UFC I'm kinda over it," Strickland wrote on X. "McGregor makes 30 million to fight for 30 seconds and they don't want to pay us a fraction of it. Contemplating just going to 205 [pounds], knocking out my contract and scrapping with [Jake Paul]. That sounds fun."

Paul, who has been vocal for years along with MVP in encouraging the UFC to increase its fighter pay, acknowledged Strickland's post in a response.

"Sean Strickland I see your texts but are you out of contract?" Paul wrote. "Tell your 'promoter' to call MVP."

stories.headline: Harry Kane interest in MLS 'fulfilment of a dream' - commissioner
stories.summary: MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.
stories.body:
MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.

The 33-year-old is in the running for the Ballon d'Or having scored 73 goals for club and country in a season that saw the striker win the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich before World Cup bronze.

Kane shows no signs of slowing and he marked his record-equalling 125th England appearance by extending his international goal tally to 91 in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win against Czechia.

The striker scored six goals across a four-match camp that began with him revealing his interest in eventually moving to MLS as the striker spoke about his dreams of being an NFL kicker.

"I'd love for him to do that," commissioner Garber said. "I think, for me, it is the fulfilment of the dream that we had to build a proper soccer league that would drive a soccer nation. That sounds colloquial but actually we have that written down.

"We wanted to create something that would have the Harry Kanes of the world say 'I'd kind of like to play in MLS.' And I think Messi proved that.

"That was a competitive process, working to ensure that we had a dynamic that would be better than going back to Barca, working a dynamic that would not have him want to play in Saudi Arabia.

"Play in Miami, have them be able to build a new stadium and have him set records and be an MVP, and then have an unbelievable goodbye [this week] from his international career."

Garber welcomes Kane's keenness to move to MLS and is eternally grateful to another England captain as he prepares to step down from the post of commissioner he has held since 1999.

Beckham's move to LA Galaxy acted as the catalyst for the league's growth, which only accelerated when the former midfielder helped form Inter Miami and sign Argentina great Messi in 2023.

"I don't think I would say one is more important than the other," Garber said of the star duo's impact.

"David put this league on the path to credibility and respect. In the prime of his career, he came to LA.

"He came into Major League Soccer and showed the world that this league can be competitive, it could be respected, it could be fun, it could have great players.

"It attracted [Thierry] Henry and many, many other players right after that, so without David there's probably no Major League Soccer.

"That being said, Major League Soccer would not be the global phenomenon and not be sort of on the hearts and minds of just about anybody in the world without Leo Messi."

Garber will become chairman at the turn of the year and is proud of his legacy with MLS, which was founded as part of the bid to hold the 1994 World Cup in a country that has just co-hosted the largest edition of the tournament.

- England Nations League takeaways: Kane makes history, Tuchel steadies ship

The 68-year-old says they have made the planet's "biggest commercial market for the sport" during that time and is excited to see how they build on firm foundations.

"We just went from a country road, now we're getting onto the highway," Garber told the Press Association. "And we've got to get better.

"We have to have a league that is more competitive, that has an ability to get into the Club World Cup and win games. Miami won one.

"Not just be there but have people think that an MLS team can compete against other clubs in the world."

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.
