stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Bucky Irving's big TNF; will Sean Payton salvage Broncos?
stories.summary: Bucky Irving had a big game to kick off Week 5, Sean Payton taking over playcalling duties for Broncos and other fantasy news of note
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 9: Bucky Irving puts up 31.5 points on TNF

By Adam Rank

Not even the Cowboys could have seen this coming from Bucky Irving.

There are a lot of people who walk around trying to pretend like they saw the twist coming in "The Sixth Sense," "Fight Club," or maybe even "Meet the Parents." That seems more plausible than people who will claim they saw the Bucky Irving game coming. Impossible. I won't believe it. This Tampa Bay Buccaneers team was baaaad. Irving had scored just over six fantasy points in the previous game. Sean Tucker was stealing touchdowns. The Buccaneers were starting an undrafted quarterback.

But, it's the Dallas Cowboys. In primetime. Perhaps we should have seen it coming?

The point is, what's done is done. Most of us likely still played Irving because there is a lack of available inventory at running back. Like walking into a Spirit Halloween in late October and trying to find a "Youth the Brat" costume. You can't do it.

So, the question of the day is, is Irving back? I don't want to be that guy in this situation, considering we're feeling so good about how well Irving played. Nobody wants to be that guy. But ...

The Buccaneers play the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6. Not a great matchup. But then they face the Carolina Panthers (amazing), Atlanta Falcons (not bad) and Chicago Bears (tough). It could be a frustrating exercise guessing where Irving pops in certain matchups and underperforms in others. Kenny Gainwell is still a factor in the passing game. Tucker had more snaps this week than last. Irving is a good RB2 option moving forward.

Here are some other notes from Thursday night:

The Cowboys allowed 241 rushing yards. Let's take a quick scan at the opponents looming on the horizon for Dallas: Green Bay Packers, Philadelphia Eagles (Will Shipley?) and Arizona Cardinals are the next three. Make your plans now for the Jeremiyah Love game.
George Pickens finally had the game many hoped for after being selected at the end of the second and early third round this summer. Pickens excelled while CeeDee Lamb battled through a quad injury. Lamb left the game in the fourth quarter. Pickens will shine if Lamb is going to miss time over the next few weeks. Ryan Flournoy is the rare receiver insurance policy. I nearly dropped him in a league this week, but thankfully I didn't follow through.
I'm sure you saw the clip of the stadium employee who said it was "embarrassing" when Dak Prescott walked down the tunnel after the game. I'm sorry, was Dak the one who set the ball to Alex Anzalone like he was Karch Kiraly? Embarrassing is a bit strong. But it is another mid performance for Prescott, who has two top-12 outings this season. I mean, he's currently No. 1 this week. Odds are it doesn't hold. And based on recent findings, he's going to end up outside of the top 12 again. The next four weeks should be good, however.

Oct. 8: Sean Payton is not a cure-all for Broncos fantasy woes

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

It'd be understandable if fantasy managers of Denver Broncos players are giddy with excitement following the news that head coach Sean Payton is taking back playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb.

These Broncos, who finished 10th in yards and 14th in scoring last season, have seen those rankings dip to 27th in either category in 2026. Bo Nix is only the No. 20 quarterback in terms of fantasy scoring, and much ballyhooed offseason acquisition Jaylen Waddle is 33th among wide receivers. And don't get any of us started on Courtland Sutton or the top two running backs, J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

But here's the reality of the situation: Playcalling changes don't always lend immediate, dramatic results, and this season's returns thus far might be as much of an indication of Nix's raw talent than it is the playcalling.

Sure, under Webb's direction, the Broncos' offense has been more conservative, forcing Nix to rely much more on dump-offs and screens. And perhaps Payton, who coaxed decently productive seasons from the 26-year-old quarterback in 2024 and 2025, will open things up more, raising Nix's ceiling for softer matchups and getting the ball to Waddle with more space to make things happen after the catch.

To the latter point, Waddle's average depth of target is down more than 2 yards this season, and he's on pace for 51 targets within 5 yards of, or behind, the line of scrimmage, which would be easily his most since his rookie season in 2021. I'd love to see him targeted more in the deep game, raising his ceiling into the mid-to-high range of fantasy WR2s, but it's hardly a guarantee that this coaching move will make it happen. Waddle is slightly more attractive as a trade target -- and this speaks to those of you off to slow starts in need of shaking things up with higher-upside moves -- but I'm not making rash adjustments to my valuations.

As is, it hasn't been the easiest of schedules for Payton's Broncos (@KC, JAX, LAR, @SF), and things do ease up with matchups against the Los Angeles Chargers (Week 5) and Arizona Cardinals (Week 7) upcoming. Denver's second-half schedule is better than the first as well. That's as much of an actionable on the trade front for Broncos players, but it's also not something that should dramatically swing the arrow upward.

Oct. 8: Week 5 stats to know
by Michael F. Florio

David Montgomery has posted career lows in yards per carry, forced missed tackles rate, explosive run rate, yards before and after contact per carry, average speed and success rate. Simply put, outside of the three TDs in Week 1, it's been rough for Monty. Wait for his next big game, which could be this week against the Tennessee Titans, and then look to trade him.
Carnell Tate's target share has climbed every week, reaching 43% in Week 4. He is being used downfield more. It seems like the Titans are unlocking him. On the season, 26 of his 32 targets have come against zone coverage, which the Houston Texans play 83% of the time.
Every QB who faced the Detroit Lions has scored at least 21 fantasy points. They have weekly finishes of QB8, QB1, QB3 and QB6. Start Jacoby Brissett this week.
Three of four QBs to face the Washington Commanders have topped 23 fantasy points. Jameis Winston is in play as a streaming option this week.
The Lions have allowed the most yards before contact per carry (2.0) and the second-highest explosive run rate (15%) to RBs. Jeremiyah Love is poised for a bounce-back performance.
Quinshon Judkins saw a career-high seven targets last week and his touches have increased every game, reaching 23 in Week 4. The New York Jets have allowed the fourth-most rushing yards per game to RBs.
Garrett Wilson has a 50% target share against man coverage, which is tied for the highest in the NFL (Amon-Ra St. Brown). The Cleveland Browns play man coverage at the highest rate in the NFL (50%).
DK Metcalf is tied for the league lead with 10 deep targets. This week he faces the Indianapolis Colts, who have allowed the most yards on deep passes.
Isaiah Likely has a 33% target share with Winston at QB. He faces the Commanders, who are in the top five in terms of most touchdowns and fantasy PPG allowed to tight ends.
Dalton Kincaid, who has just five targets and 45 yards in his last two games combined, faces the Los Angeles Rams who have allowed a league-low 85 yards to tight ends this season and just one touchdown.

Oct. 7: Trade for or trade away? SOS says make these six moves today

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

We're at that time of season where the fantasy football trade market is either heating up or is already at peak temperature.

There's inevitably a 0-4 team in your league, grasping to hopes of a miracle comeback. And it can be done, especially if I remind you that all you probably need is a 7-3 hot streak to make the playoffs as an I-sure-don't-want-to-face-them No. 4 seed. Trades -- especially bigger, badder and bolder ones -- are the best way to turn around a slow start.

One way to unearth the highest-ceiling trades is to lean heavily upon the upcoming schedule. Mix and match your way into the playoffs and be that maddening team to face! This week, Mike Clay has released his initial version of the rest-of-season schedule rankings at each position -- kickers and defenses, too!

It's a great tool for determining how fluky your player's extreme hot-or-cold start to the season might have been, as well as which players are in the best positions to thrive over the remaining 13 weeks of the fantasy season.

Here are six trade-related takeaways to consider as you start offering deals:

Bryce Young has been an unexpected early breakthrough, going from a No. 186 overall ADP and 11.1% opening-week roster rate to scoring the third-most fantasy points among quarterbacks through four weeks. He has certainly capitalized upon a soft schedule, the seventh-best at the position thus far. Young and his Carolina Panthers are on bye, but they have the position's third toughest the rest of the year. Young might be a tough player to trade based upon his past history, but considering his schedule and how bruised and battered the quarterback position on the whole, he's a name worth floating if you're confident in your QB1.
He might seem like an unappealing fantasy RB2, but Aaron Jones Sr. could be one of the sneakiest running back values amongst that valuation tier, particularly over the next six weeks. Since Jordan Mason landed on IR, Jones' 78% snap and 73% rushing shares both rank fourth, and his 41.5 fantasy points are 14th, among running backs. Jones and the Minnesota Vikings also face the third most-favorable remaining schedule at the position, including nothing but upper-half matchups (aside from a Week 6 bye) the next seven weeks (@NO, bye, IND, @DET, BUF, @GB, @SF).
Colston Loveland's fantasy managers are surely displeased after the No. 37 overall pick in terms of ADP has placed just 19th in target share (14.9%) and 31st in fantasy points (20.1) among tight ends through four weeks. His Chicago Bears' remaining schedule offers some hope of recovering TE1 value, as theirs has been the third toughest at the position thus far but the third most-favorable the rest of the year. Examining alternatives, I can't find more than five tight ends (Trey McBride, Brock Bowers, George Kittle, Tyler Warren and Sam LaPorta) I'd clearly prefer to Loveland the rest of the year.
It's difficult to envision Christian McCaffrey having as strong a finish as he had in 2025. The San Francisco 49ers have been more conservative with his workload through four weeks in 2026 (67% snap and 43% rushing shares) than at the same point in 2025 (83% and 65%), and he faces the most challenging remaining schedule among running backs. This isn't to persuade McCaffrey's managers to swiftly trade him for whatever they can get, but rather to caution that he might fall shy of expectations. Adjust your running back plan accordingly.
The hype surrounding Trevor Lawrence exiting Week 1 has dissipated, but there's still a lot to like about him and his receivers moving forward. Remember, Lawrence scored the second-most fantasy points among all players (and the most among quarterbacks) from Week 5 forward last year, and two of his toughest matchups all year are already in the rearview (Week 2-3's @DEN, NE). Between him and 2-fantasy-points-in-Week 4 WR Parker Washington, they're among my favorite trade targets right now.
The Seahawks' defense has again excelled early, their 40 fantasy points second among D/STs. What lies ahead, though, is the worst schedule for a defense, including two games apiece against the Los Angeles Rams and 49ers, and single meetings with the Kansas City Chiefs, Chicago Bears and Dallas Cowboys. Here's your almost daily reminder: Stream defenses!

Oct. 6: Jalen Hurts' job gets a lot tougher with Lane Johnson retirement

By Michael F. Florio

Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL on Tuesday. That will leave a massive hole on the offensive line for an Eagles team that is missing a ton of star players. Saquon Barkley hurt a hamstring, and he is expected to miss Week 5. DeVonta Smith was out last week due to a hamstring injury, and he seems unlikely for Week 5. And Dallas Goedert remains sidelined with a knee injury.

Jalen Hurts has struggled in games without Johnson, having averaged 174 passing yards and 1.1 passing touchdowns per game when Johnson sat. On top of that, the quarterback faces a Jacksonville Jaguars team that has allowed three passing touchdowns and has six interceptions this season. Jacksonville can get after the QB, as well, producing 10 sacks through four weeks, eighth most in the NFL. That's problematic without Johnson.

Perhaps Hurts' rushing ability saves the day, but he has not ran as much this season. He has fewer than 20 rushing yards in two of his past three games and one rushing touchdown this campaign. Plus, the Jaguars have allowed the second-fewest rushing yards and just two rushing touchdowns so far in 2026.

Some QBs I would play over Hurts are Matthew Stafford, Jacoby Brissett, Kyler Murray and Jordan Love. The "floors" here are not safe, but Jameis Winston and Aaron Rodgers are upside options this week in favorable matchups.

Falcons' offense has come alive under Michael Penix Jr.

By Michael F. Florio

The Atlanta Falcons are hitting their stride with Michael Penix Jr. They scored 45 points Monday night against the New Orleans Saints and have 80 total in Penix's two starts. Penix threw for 223 yards and one touchdown, finishing with 12.72 fantasy points. He has yet to crack 15 and is primarily a superflex option, although all the QB injuries could change that.

Penix's impact on the Falcons offense cannot be overstated. Bijan Robinson went for 147 total yards and two touchdowns Monday, and in 16 career games with Penix at the helm he has 2,181 scrimmage yards and 17 touchdowns. Robinson saves his best for primetime, which means fantasy managers are in luck, as the Falcons play the Baltimore Ravens on "Sunday Night Football" next week.

Penix also continues to elevate Drake London. After going for 194 yards in Week 3, London was held to a modest 96 yards on five catches Monday. He has 105 catches, 1,576 yards and nine touchdowns in 16 career games with Penix. He has to be viewed as an elite fantasy option as long as Penix is healthy.

And Brian Robinson Jr. had himself a night, turning 15 opportunities into 67 yards and three touchdowns. He has double-digit touches in each of his past three games and has four total touchdowns in the past two games. Robinson should be added off the waiver wire if he is out there. Not only is he one of the top insurance backs, but he is carving out a role with standalone value. He can be a flex option with byes coming up and due to all the injuries.

What else you need to know from 'Monday Night Football':

Chris Olave continues to produce at an extremely high level. He turned 12 targets into eight catches for 116 yards Monday and has topped 19 fantasy points in every game. Outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Amon-Ra St. Brown, there are not many receivers I would rather have.
It was a tough game for Tyler Shough, who was able to salvage his fantasy night with a last-drive touchdown pass. He finished with 286 yards and the touchdown, failing to top 22 fantasy points for the first time this season (15.94). Still, Shough is in play outside of the tough matchups. But he has just that next week against the Minnesota Vikings, so fantasy managers may want to look at their other options.
Alvin Kamara led the way in the backfield for the Saints with 41% of the snaps, posting seven carries and seven targets. He turned those into 58 yards and two touchdowns. While it is tough to bank on big yardage from Kamara, the pass-game work paired with goal-line usage keeps him in play as a RB2 or flex option.
Juwan Johnson and Devaughn Vele continue to produce for the Saints. Johnson turned eight targets into six catches for 59 yards. He has double-digit fantasy points in every game and is the TE3 on the season. He has earned his way into starting lineups weekly. Vele finished with six catches, 54 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. He has topped 11 fantasy points three times. Vele is a high-floor option who can be started most weeks until rookie Jordyn Tyson returns.
Kendre Miller fumbled and the Saints turned to rookie CJ Donaldson late. While Kamara is the only Saints RB you can use for fantasy right now, this RB2 battle is one to monitor moving forward.

stories.headline: UEFA member nations call FIFA's international break a 'disaster'
stories.summary: European soccer federations told UEFA they are not happy with the new extended four-game blocks of international matches that finished this week.
stories.body:
European federations told UEFA they are not happy with the new extended four-game blocks of international matches that finished this week.

Injured players like Kylian Mbappé missed too many games, Erling Haaland asked to come off in Norway's fourth match, resources were stretched for coaches in smaller countries and extra demands were made on the time and money of fans and sponsors.

A "disaster," said one official among multiple federations who spoke to The Associated Press on the sidelines of a closed-doors UEFA meeting Thursday in Berlin. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the confidential debate.

UEFA said it will gather their views to weigh a submission to FIFA about the 16-day block that combined what used to be separate two-game breaks in September and October.

Still, the four-game early-season block is locked in for four more years on the FIFA-managed calendar for international matches that is finalized through 2030. That year national teams in Europe will play four games between Sept. 23 to Oct. 8. Next year they will be qualifying games for the 2028 European Championship.

Fewer but longer breaks for international games have long been wanted by European clubs seeking to limit disruption to their seasons, and cut long-haul travel for their players from outside the continent.

Still, the past three weeks have not been popular with one Champions League club, whose coach led his national team Croatia for two years including at the 2014 World Cup.

"We now have the issue of not only having the occasional player coming back injured, but also the fact you go two or 2½ weeks without any momentum," Borussia Dortmund coach Niko Kovač said this week. "We're all starting from scratch now, in a sense."

Outside of Europe, FIFA has said the longer break allowed time for regional tournaments like the eight-team Arabian Gulf Cup played Sept. 23-Oct. 6 in Saudi Arabia.

FIFA pushed to condense international breaks in 2021 as part of its biennial World Cup proposal, and later updated its calendar for men's football.

The calendar mandates when clubs must release players for international duty, including the World Cup, where FIFA pays hundreds of millions of dollars to clubs worldwide whose players represented their national teams.

After the UEFA meeting Thursday, officials said only Azerbaijan among the 55 member federations spoke out in clear defense of FIFA's management of the calendar.

The four-game break followed two months after the longest-ever World Cup, the first with 48 teams and where Norway played into July after reaching the quarterfinals.

"For those who play in the Champions League and have had little vacation, it's more brutal than for the others," Norway coach Stale Solbakken said of the schedule and after substituting Haaland in the second half of a loss Sunday to Portugal.

Haaland faces an intense week with Manchester City, going to Liverpool on Sunday in the Premier League then hosting Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday.

European national teams next call up players for camps starting Nov. 9 to play two games that complete the Nations League group phase.

stories.headline: How to ace your salary cap draft: Tips and strategies to build a winning team
stories.summary: Are you ready for your salary cap draft? Jim McCormick lays out helpful strategies and tactics you can use to ace draft day.
stories.body:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is undeniably awesome. So is Victor Wembanyama. Yet, in a traditional snake draft, getting both is essentially impossible given both are found firmly in the first round.

There is a draft format, however, that absolutely allows you to pair SGA and Wemby. Or Nikola Jokic and Stephen Curry, Luka Doncic and Giannis Antetokounmpo ... you get the idea. Salary cap drafts afford you the ability to assemble compelling collections of superstars.

The mission of this piece isn't solely to explain how salary cap drafting works, but more importantly, share several actionable strategies to help you thrive in this uniquely rewarding way to build fantasy basketball rosters.

How a Salary Cap drafts work
In ESPN salary cap drafts, each manager begins with a $200 budget to build out their roster. Default settings host 13 roster spots, with the calculator on my laptop revealing this is a bit more than $15 per slot. You are welcome, of course, to spend well above $15 to acquire star-caliber players, leaving less for filler and depth.

Instead of having a fixed draft slot to acquire NBA talent as you would in a snake draft, managers rotate turns nominating players for bidding. As you might guess, the highest bidder when the clock hits zero lands that player on their respective roster. As my long-time colleague John Cregan once coined, "your reign as manager begins with a wad of fake cash, a couple of hours to kill, and an empty roster to stock."

Now that we have an idea how they operate, let's delve into some winning tips for salary cap drafts. The road to imaginary glory begins here.

Preparation pays
Leverage live draft trends as you prepare for your salary cap draft. Just like how we identify average draft position as a tool of differentiation and value in snake drafts, average salary performs this function in this format.

Unlike how we enter snake drafts knowing that certain players will get drafted in a finite range of selections, the variance and volatility of player pricing inherent to a salary draft demands you identify which players you truly want to target with your imaginary coin.

Which is to say, set not only price ranges you are willing to pay (within a few dollars) for specific NBA talents, but order players into pricing tiers.

If you are the turn in a snake draft, your options are almost surely limited to a handful of top talents available in that range. In salary formats, you can acquire two typical first-rounders, or four players generally found in the second and third rounds of snake results.

Before such expenditure, just make sure to have identified which talents in each tier you intend to bid for. In category-driven leagues, it's wise to prepare lists of players who thrive in distinct statistical categories; knowing that Cason Wallace is an elite, underrated source of steals. Or that Myles Turner can drive bold block results without tanking free-throw efficiency. No matter the scoring key, it's beneficial to list your top targets at each position, as well.

Preparation is more crucial and comes with greater rewards in salary drafts, as average draft position doesn't do the work for you.

Be nimble
While snake drafts can throw some surprises at you; a reach here, a player sliding there, salary formats are atypical in that each draft room behaves as its own unique market. Did the room hesitate to pay enough for a top star who is coming off a down season? Maybe he goes $15 or so below expected value, but that doesn't necessarily equate to a trend, as there could be a bidding war for him in another salary draft.

Value is a variant concept in these drafts, so being adaptive and nimble is critical. This is why we can refer back to preparation; if you establish your targets at different tiers, statistics, and positions, then you'll be ready to act on players who appear undervalued in that specific salary market. Players closer to the end of a tier, or round using snake results as a comparison, are often where bargains emerge.

Come up a strategy ... or multiple strategies
There are a bevy of established investing strategies to consider for salary cap drafts. I don't believe it's prudent to lock into any one of these prior to the first nomination, but it does help to have an understanding of how some early decisions might dictate your path. Let's consider a few of the more notable approaches.

The freedom of salary drafting bears the need for restraint in order to refine and define your strategy and player valuations. You determine which players best fit your philosophy, rather than a draft spot you often randomly net in snake rooms.

Stars and sleepers
If you've identified strong interest in Luka and Giannis in your pre-draft prep and they both appear undervalued as the bidding approaches the final seconds, go for it. Just be mindful this pairing would still likely consume 60% of your total budget, leaving say $80 of your original $200 to canvass the remaining roster spots. Sometimes, as the early bidding begins, the superstars find you.

Pro basketball is a space where heliocentric stars often drive impressive outcomes even with role players riding shotgun, as both Luka and Giannis' actual NBA careers confirm, so you can make this strategy of extremes work. It will just demand savvy waiver management and securing some sleepers in the draft.

Snake style
It's unlikely that anyone actually calls this strategy "snake style," but I just did. The premise here is simple: you can mimic a snake-draft outcome by targeting one true high-dollar star -- or, in this comparison, a first-round talent. In current live draft trends, that can mean roughly $80 for the Joker and Wemby, or about $35 for the likes of Karl-Anthony Towns and Amen Thompson. Assume downshifts in spending with each successive tier.

Minding the middle
I generally don't adhere to the aforementioned snake-like framework, as the power of salary drafts is the ability to identify, for instance, that you love the values found in the third-to-fifth rounds, allowing you to load up on say five of such players. Then again, it's up to you how to navigate your spending.

My most common approach; netting one high-dollar star and complementing them with a series of those mid-round gems we all admire. An example this year would include paying top-dollar for statistical anchors like Victor Wembanyama or Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and then focusing on the likes of Austin Reaves, Coby White, Cameron Boozer, and Nickeil Alexander-Walker at prices below what I project and expect their actual production will deliver.

Draft with discipline
Sticking to your pre-game planning in regards to player targets, tiers and statistical specialists is far more vital than adhering to any of the approaches such as stars or sleepers or snake-driven spending. It's also important to note that you avoid what we nerds deem as price enforcing; engaging in bidding almost purely to protect the price point of a specific or multiple players.

This is how you end up spending real percentages of your budget on players you truly didn't want just an hour before the draft. There is a very clear line between identifying a value and trying to police every bid. Your peers will absolutely get some great values during the process, but your team is paramount to those outcomes.

There really should be a breaking point for when you stop bidding, just as you should feel comfortable trusting your pre-draft price points with regards to paying enough for talent you want on your team.

After all, you will ride with many of your choices for months during the NBA marathon, so at least you can enjoy the team you wanted all along.

stories.headline: 2026 WNBA semifinals: Can Las Vegas and New York avoid elimination?
stories.summary: Eliminations are on the line for both WNBA playoff semifinal Game 3s. What does each team need to focus on?
stories.body:
The Las Vegas Aces have won three of the past four WNBA championships, and the other one went to the New York Liberty. But both teams now are in playoff peril, down 0-2 in their best-of-five semifinals series. They will try to keep their seasons alive Friday when they host Game 3s.

The Liberty face the Atlanta Dream (7:30 p.m. ET, ESPN2) at Barclays Center. The Dream have won nine straight overall and four in a row against the Liberty, going back to the last week of the regular season. Atlanta won the first two games of this series 92-82 and 101-98 in overtime.

The Aces went 3-0 against the Golden State Valkyries in the regular season but are in danger of being swept in the semifinals. They hope to turn things around in Game 3 (9:30 p.m. ET) after losing 71-60 and 83-81 in San Francisco.

Atlanta has made three WNBA Finals appearances but was swept in each. Golden State, an expansion team in just its second season, lost in the first round last year.

The Aces' A'ja Wilson (five MVPs) and the Liberty's Breanna Stewart (two MVPs) are superstars used to winning championships. But they will need to pull their teams out of huge holes to have the chance to play for the 2026 title. No WNBA team has come back to win a best-of-five series after being down 0-2.

Jump to:

New York | Las Vegas

Atlanta | Golden State

How can New York get a win Friday and keep its season alive?

Voepel: The Liberty have to hit the reset button, joke intended. That means getting Wednesday's end-of-overtime chaos out of their heads. It's understandable if they were irritated by the officials (and their own coaching staff) about the confusion on the reset timeout that the Liberty had but didn't use. But even if they had taken it, there's no guarantee they would have hit the tying 3-pointer or won in the second overtime.
Along with resetting, the Liberty have to hold on to the ball. Even with Atlanta guard Allisha Gray playing just 11 minutes of Game 1 and missing all of Game 2 because of a finger injury, the Dream have dictated pace and forced game-changing turnovers. Atlanta has scored 20-plus points off turnovers in all of its playoff games so far, becoming the first team in WNBA history to do that in four consecutive postseason games.

Copeland: Michael couldn't be more right when it comes to the turnovers. It's such a simple correlation. Too simple to be blamed alone, but it's absolutely glaring. Game 1: 21 turnovers led to 32 points in a game the Liberty lost by 10. Game 2: 17 turnovers led to 28 points in a game they lost by three. Plus, a big turnover at the worst possible time.

The friendly confines of the Barclays Center should settle things down a bit, though a veteran-led squad wasn't expected to let a road environment have that drastic of an effect. But this is an aggressive Dream defense that led the league in steals this season.

How can Las Vegas avoid elimination Friday?

Copeland: I thought the Aces' experience and high-level of offensive playmaking would be able to neutralize the No. 1 defense in the league, but that hasn't happened through 80 minutes. There's one thing, though, that the Aces can't have regardless of whether they're playing the Valkyries or any other playoff team -- Jackie Young averaging 12.5 points. Now, this isn't pointing the finger at Young; the Aces have had a lot of issues in this series, but she's a five-time All-Star and two-time all-WNBA selection who was a top-10 scorer with a career-high 18.9 points per game in the regular season. Her unique ability as a three-level scorer is a huge reason the Aces have three titles. They're just not the same dominant team when she's shooting a combined 6-for-22 through two games.

Voepel: Let's start with rebounding. Coach Becky Hammon thought that -- along with every other aspect of Las Vegas' play -- was terrible in Game 1 as the Valkyries had a 52-25 edge on the boards. She said the Aces' rebounding in Game 2 -- 30-25 for the Valkyries -- was better but not good enough.
The Aces (33.4 rebounds per game) and Valkyries (33.3) were almost identical in rebounding during the regular season. Of course, Las Vegas was affected by losing starting forward NaLyssa Smith (6.4 rebounds per game) to a knee injury Aug. 23.

What really stood out, especially in Game 1, was the Aces being beaten on "hustle" rebounds, as the Valkyries seemed to play harder. Golden State coach Natalie Nakase said she expected the Aces to play with a lot more aggression in Game 2, and they did.

But that leads to another problem for Las Vegas: shooting. The Aces shot 34% in Game 1 for a season-low 60 points. It was up to 44% for Game 2, but they struggled in the first quarter and trailed by 11 at halftime. The Aces expended a lot of energy just getting back into the game Wednesday, and even when they did, Golden State made enough big plays near the end to hold on to the victory.

There's no doubt the Aces miss Smith and Jewell Loyd (leg), who was injured in Game 1. But if they want to keep their hopes alive for another title, they have to dictate pace, rebound, make shots and play with a sense of desperation.

How can Atlanta close out the series?

Voepel: Along with the aforementioned points they've scored off turnovers, the Dream have had balanced scoring in both games against New York. In the opener, four Atlanta players had at least 16 points, led by Jordin Canada's 25. In Game 2, Canada and Angel Reese led six players in double figures with 23 points. Canada's scoring is just one aspect of her impact; she has also totaled 12 assists and six steals against the Liberty. It might be tough for Atlanta to finish off a sweep in Brooklyn, especially if Gray is still unable to play. But the Dream have positioned themselves well to win the series even if it isn't a sweep.

How can Golden State complete the sweep?

Copeland: Continue to find timely offensive help off the bench. The question going into the series was whether the Valkyries could generate enough offense. Then Aminata Gueye and Kaitlyn Chen combined for 20 points off the bench in Game 1 and Tiffany Hayes contributed 21 points, one shy of her 2026 regular-season high, off the bench in just 16 minutes in Game 2. The team's depth is often discussed on the defensive end, but it has played a significant role throughout these playoffs.

Voepel: If you had a nickel for every time we've talked this season about Golden State's defense, you would have yourself a nice little pile of change. But how can we not talk about it? Admittedly, the Aces' three regular-season victories against the Valkyries came in May and June, when Las Vegas still had a healthy Smith. But after she was injured in the Aces' Aug. 23 game, Las Vegas still won seven games in a row and eight of its last nine before facing Golden State. And then things came to a halt.

Hammon was disgusted by all aspects of the Aces' effort in Game 1, but the Valkyries hounded them into that. A Golden State player might not have gotten the Defensive Player of the Year award, as that went to Atlanta's Reese. But the Valkryies are the defensive team of the year, with players such as Gabby Williams and Veronica Burton able to guard a wide range of sizes and types of players throughout the game. Then there's Kiah Stokes, who stood between Chelsea Gray and the potential tying basket in Game 2. Previously a valuable member of the Aces for her defense, she now does that for Golden State. And this is not to shortchange the rest of the Valkyries' defenders, because as good as the sum of the parts are, the whole is even better. If they play Game 3 the same way, they could grab their spot in the Finals.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Rangers, Capitals square off in early Metro showdown

stories.body:
After the megameal on Thursday -- with 10 contests -- it's lighter fare on Friday around the NHL, as just four games dot the landscape.

Here's a look at the key stats and storylines in each contest, along with betting info on broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Seattle Kraken at Detroit Red Wings

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DET -142, O/U: 5.5

With low expectations heading into this season, the Kraken have shown some life, and have two wins to show for it. The Red Wings have been a bit more uneven, but did earn a W in Dylan Larkin's first game back following a trade request and a stint on injured reserve. If there's any bad blood or unsettled scores following the final horn, there's good news: the two teams meet again in Seattle on Oct. 20.

New York Rangers at Washington Capitals

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | WSH -142, O/U: 5.5

Based on the preseason futures markets, there was a fair amount of Capitals believers out there -- but not so many felt the same way about the Rangers. Nevertheless, the Blueshirts persisted, rocketing to the top of the Metro Division after the first 10 days, with just one loss and a plus-8 goal differential. The Caps will be looking to land an early-season body blow to their division rivals, and feature the kind of roster that can do so: they have the NHL's heaviest roster (average weight: 93.96 kilograms or 205 pounds) and the fourth tallest (average height: 188.17 cm or 6-foot-2).

Pittsburgh Penguins at Columbus Blue Jackets

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CBJ -125, O/U: 6.5

One of the NHL's underrated rivalries, with just 185 miles between the cities. The franchises have met twice in the playoffs, with the Penguins winning each time (4-2 in 2014 and 4-1 in 2017). Given the strength of the rest of the Eastern Conference, these teams could very well be battling well into April for one last spot. The winner of this game will get two points that count just as much in the standings as those "pivotal" games down the stretch.

Anaheim Ducks at Winnipeg Jets

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | WPG -125, O/U: 6.5

After a thrilling return to the postseason in 2026, the Ducks were expected by many to be a strong contender to return. The Jets -- having missed the playoffs by a mile, and without star goalie Connor Hellebuyck -- had fewer backers. But, that's why they play the games! The Jets have roared to a 3-0-1 record, good for a tie with Edmonton atop the Western Conference. Which team soars higher in this one?

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.
stories.body:
With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.

Determining when and where that coronation will likely take place is much harder to say, not least because there are still question marks over how many races remain in the F1 calendar.

Antonelli's closest competitor, Mercedes teammate George Russell, saw his title chances take a critical blow when he retired from Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with an engine failure, and a related grid penalty at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix will make his job tougher still.

Meanwhile, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris and Max Verstappen all remain in mathematical contention for this year's championship, but face even tougher routes to the title than Russell due to their greater points deficits.

When could Antonelli win his first title?
In theory, the earliest Antonelli could seal the title is at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin later this month. In order to do so, he would need to grow his gap over Russell by 42 points in two race weekends, while outscoring Lewis Hamilton in third place by 20 points.

- Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch

- Valtteri Bottas cycles 400km from Malaysia to Singapore

- F1 cars to get software update after Malaysia 'bug'

Even with extra points on offer at the sprint race in Singapore this weekend, such a scenario would likely require victories for Antonelli and further retirements for Russell, while ensuring Hamilton is not in the fight for second place on the podium behind Antonelli. In addition, an Austin crowning would require Antonelli to make sure he is not outscored by three points by Leclerc, and six points by both Norris and Verstappen.

What does Antonelli need to claim the title?
Perhaps the easiest way to look at Antonelli's title run-in is that he needs to score 100 points over the remaining races to ensure he ends up as champion -- regardless of what any of his rivals manage.

With seven grands prix and a sprint race currently scheduled on the calendar, that route could be achieved with multiple different result combinations -- but for ease of an example, third place at every remaining race would comfortably see Antonelli over the line even if Russell wins at all seven grands prix and the sprint.

F1's rules state that if multiple drivers are tied on points, a countback of victories will decide who emerges on top. If the number of victories are also even, it then goes to second places, third places, fourth place, and so on. Currently, Antonelli has eight victories to Russell's three, although Russell has four second places to Antonelli's three. It's unlikely those countbacks will come into play, but it's why, currently, Antonelli needs 100 points rather than 99 to put the title entirely beyond Russell's grasp.

But how many races are actually left?
The situation is further complicated by question marks hanging over the final two races of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. F1 has made clear that it intends to finish the season as scheduled, but the ongoing war between the United States and Iran has the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

The same conflict led the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in April, while Bahrain took the unusual approach of hosting its round 4,000 miles away from the island kingdom in Malaysia last weekend.

If Qatar and Abu Dhabi are also cancelled, F1's contingency plan is to host the final round of the season in Imola. Such a scenario would remove 25 of the potential points on offer, meaning Antonelli would only need 75 points between now and the end of the season to be crowned champion. Austin would still be the earliest round at which he could clinch the title, but it would come with a more achievable target of outscoring Russell by 17 points across the Singapore and U.S. race weekends rather than 42.

stories.headline: Saints AFLW coach steps down as club plans review
stories.summary: Embattled St Kilda AFLW coach Nick Dal Santo has stepped down amid the club's winless season.
stories.body:
Embattled St Kilda AFLW coach Nick Dal Santo has stepped down amid the club's winless season.

The last-placed Saints will conduct a review into their AFLW program, led by former Carlton football boss Brad Lloyd, in the wake of Dal Santo's departure.

Dal Santo, a St Kilda great as a player, was in his sixth season at the Saints and will coach his final game against Collingwood on Saturday, before departing.

"I've been giving a lot of thought to my future and whether continuing in this role was the right decision, both for myself and the program," Dal Santo said in a statement.

"Where we've been able to take this program is something I'll always be incredibly proud of.

"It's been a privilege to coach this group and help shape its formative years in the competition.

"I have a strong love for this club, I wanted to contribute to women's football, and with a daughter of my own, it's great to see a pathway for young females with football ambitions.

"I'm looking forward to finishing my time as coach alongside the group this weekend and wish them every success for what comes next."

The Saints will have three games left in the season after Saturday, when they will attempt to amend their unwanted record of being the only winless team in the competition.

"Nick has made a significant contribution to our AFLW program across six seasons and will always be an important part of our football club," St Kilda chief executive Carl Dilena said in a statement

"His care, commitment and leadership have been unwavering, and we thank him for everything he has given to the program, including leading the team to its maiden final's appearance last season.

"We look forward to recognising Nick's contribution this weekend as he leads the team one final time in front of our members and supporters at RSEA Park."

Lloyd will lead the review, via Apogee Sports, during the remainder of the season, while the Saints start their hunt for their next coach.

"Our ambition is to be a consistently competitive and respected club that can contend with the best in the competition," Dilena said.

"We want to give our AFLW program every chance to achieve this and that means identifying where we need to improve, investing in the right areas and acting with urgency."

stories.headline: Silva rises in P4P women's top 10, making most of golden opportunity
stories.summary: After winning UFC women's flyweight title, Silva rises in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
The women's flyweight division might be the most stacked weight class in the UFC, and Natalia Silva wears the gold.

Silva was too fast, too precise and too elusive for Wang Cong in the UFC 332 main event on Saturday, and as a result, the 29-year-old from Brazil captured the vacant 125-pound title. She moves up one position to No. 4 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

Silva is one of seven flyweights in the women's top 10. The division with the next most pound-for-pound elites is lightweight, with three fighters in the men's rankings.

The top two fighters on the women's list are Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the UFC title last month while healing shoulder and back injuries, and Zhang Weili, a two-time former strawweight titlist who last fought at flyweight, in an unsuccessful challenge of Shevchenko in November.

Aside from Silva, there are three other UFC flyweights in the top 10 (Alexa Grasso, Manon Fiorot and Erin Blanchfield), and the rankings also include PFL 125-pounder Dakota Ditcheva.

UFC women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has been missing from these rankings for the past few months because, with no fights since June 2025, she is ineligible. But Harrison will return from neck surgery to defend her title against former two-division champion and consensus GOAT Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Nov. 14.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Oct. 7. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which Natalia Silva captured by beating Wang Cong at UFC 332. When Shevchenko is healed up, she'll be looking to take back the belt.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Previous ranking: 4

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her upcoming bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Cris Cyborg; 6. Alexa Grasso; 7. Manon Fiorot; 8. Dakota Ditcheva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Zhang; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Blanchfield; 10. Suarez.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

stories.headline: New Zealand Rugby launches legal action against ARLC over 'Chiefs' name
stories.summary: The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.
stories.body:
The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.

NZR on Thursday said it had been left with no choice but to launch legal proceedings against the ARLC, who has sought to adopt the name for its Papua New Guinea expansion franchise.

The PNG Chiefs are due to join the NRL in 2028 and have already signed a raft of players, including code-hoppers Zac Lomaz and Joey Manu, but they may yet have to undergo a chanGe of name if NZR gets its way.

The Chiefs' Super Rugby franchise has existed since 1996, with NZR claiming the introduction of the PNG Chiefs would result in "significant confusion and damage" should they be allowed to compete under the name from 2028.

"New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has today moved to protect the Chiefs brand and is filing proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand against the decision by the Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) to launch a new NRL side using "Chiefs" in its name," an NZR statement read.  

"NZR is seeking both an interim and final injunction which stops the use of the names 'PNG Chiefs', 'Chiefs' or any other similar names in New Zealand.   

"The Chiefs have competed as a professional rugby team in Super Rugby since 1996 and over those 30 years, have built a strong identity and fanbase across New Zealand, Australia and internationally.  

"In New Zealand, NZR owns both the trademark rights for the word Chiefs and the Chiefs logo and since 1998, NZR has also held trademark protection for the Chiefs logo in Australia."

NZR claims it had tried to engage with the ARLC in an attempt to find a resolution, yet the commission was now intent on proceeding with the official launch of the PNG Chiefs on Oct. 21.

"For 30 years the Chiefs and their players have built an incredibly strong identity that is widely recognised and loved by fans," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "We have raised our concerns with the ARLC directly and consistently over the last year in attempting to find a resolution. We now have a responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand.   

"We want to be absolutely clear, this is not about rugby league's growth in the Pacific. We welcome the development of the Pacific region through sport and the passion that the people of Papua New Guinea have for both rugby and rugby league."  

The Chiefs won two Super Rugby titles in back-to-back seasons in 2012 and 2013, and were runners-up in Super Rugby Pacific this season after suffering a crushing defeat by the Hurricanes in the decider.

The Hamilton-based team has produced countless All Blacks since its inception, with Saturday's run-on team to face the Wallabies featuring six players from the franchise.

"Here in New Zealand, when people hear 'the Chiefs', they think of this club and this region. The identity carries significant cultural meaning and connection to the region and its people, we know it means a great deal to our players and coaches past and present, fans and supporters here and around the world," Chiefs CEO Simon Graafhuis said.   

"Teams in different sports and markets can exist alongside one another with the same name, but the issue here is the similarity of our sports competing in the same market, for the same fans, in overlapping windows."  

However, ARLC executive chairman Peter V'Landys later issued a stinging rebuke, insisting he would vigorously defend PNG's right to use the Chiefs as its team name.

"The hypocrisy is mind-blowing, considering the Auckland Blues in 1996 used the NSW Blues name without any consultation or approval. The NSW Blues had been the Blues for in excess of 50 years before that," he said.

"Rugby union is obviously feeling threatened by rugby league in New Zealand, with sell-outs at most rugby league games."

No date has yet been slated for the hearing in New Zealand's High Court.
